inline_prompts: You are given a tree with NK vertices. The vertices are numbered 1,2,\dots,NK, and the i-th edge (i=1,2,\dots,NK-1) connects vertices u_i and v_i. Determine whether this tree can be decomposed into N paths, each of length K. More precisely, determine whether there exists an N \times K matrix P satisfying the following: Standard convention applies here (follow the literal input/output format given); no special handling beyond what's stated is required. For each i=1,2,\dots,N and j=1,2,\dots,K-1, there is an edge connecting vertices P_{i,j} and P_{i,j+1}. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N K u_1 v_1 u_2 v_2 \vdots u_{NK-1} v_{NK-1} Output If it is possible to decompose the tree into N paths each of length K, print Yes. Otherwise, print No. Constraints - 1 \leq N - 1 \leq K - NK \leq 2 \times 10^5 - 1 \leq u_i < v_i \leq NK - The given graph is a tree. - All input values are integers.
